ops.title: index.walk misses the primary checkout when a registered worktree is deleted
ops.description:
Found 2026-07-30 while verifying the v0.50.0 release. NOT release-blocking:
nothing outside internal/index imports the package yet, so the resolver has zero
production consumers until Phase D step 4+ wires the daemon to it.

The real ~/.cc-notes registry entry for this repo reads:

    {"common_dir":"/Users/yasyf/Code/cc-notes/.git",
     "worktrees":["/Users/yasyf/Code/cc-notes/.claude/worktrees/wf_3cbdf170-a30-2"]}

That worktree no longer exists — it was an agent worktree, registered because
`init` last ran from inside it. The primary checkout is not in the list.

internal/index/resolve.go:110-125 `walk` then fails for cwd
/Users/yasyf/Code/cc-notes: neither worktrees[dir] nor commonDirs[dir] matches
(commonDirs is keyed on .../.git, which the walk never visits), and
isBoundary() stops the climb at the first dir containing .git. Result:
ErrUnknownRepo for the repo's own primary checkout.

Also consider: the walk should match a dir whose .git resolves to a known
common_dir, so a stale worktrees list degrades instead of failing.

Related: the reaper the Phase D plan assigns to the daemon ("sweep entries whose
recorded common dir no longer resolves as a git repo") does not exist yet, so
orphaned entries accumulate. Two /tmp-repo orphans from this session's testing
were removed by hand.

ops.text: a repo registered from a worktree that is later deleted still resolves from its primary checkout
registration merges worktrees instead of recording only the registering one, and includes the primary worktree
table test covers primary-checkout, linked-worktree, deleted-worktree and bare-repo cwds
